simple.meaning: חַכָּה (chakkâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a hook (as adhering ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 40:25. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חַכָּה (H2443) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: חַכָּה (chakkâh) / H2443 is traced through Job 40:25, Isaiah 19:8, Habakkuk 1:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H2443. chakkah חַכָּה noun feminine hook fastened in jaw , fish-hook (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic חַכְּתָא ) — absolute ׳ח Job 40:25 2 t.; — חַכָּ֑ה בַיְאֹר כָּלמַֿשְׁלִיכֵי Isa 19:8 (|| הַדַּיָּגִים ), הֵעֲלָה בְּחַכָּה כֻּלֹה Hab 1:15 (of אדם , who, 1:14 , is compare to הַיָּם דְּגֵּי , and רֶמֶשׂ ), compare בְּחַכָּ֑ה לִוְיָתָן תִּמְשֹׁךְ Job 40:25. חִנָּם see below חנן

occurrences.englishText: The fishermen will lament, and all those who fish in the Nile will mourn, and those who spread nets on the waters will languish.
He takes up all of them with the hook. He catches them in his net, and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.
